critical_code_review_comments: CinemaStudio.js line 22: loadProds() uses .catch(() => {}) which silently swallows errors. If /api/cinema-studio/productions ever fails, the panel will show the empty-state 'No productions yet.' with no indication of the failure. Consider surfacing a small error chip or toast so the Founder isn't confused.

CinemaStudio.js line 30-43: manufacture() has no client-side timeout guard; a video manufacture that hangs for >2 minutes will keep the button spinner infinite. axios default timeout applies but a UX-level cancel/timeout with a friendly toast would be safer.

The pre-manufacture toast on video path (line 33-35) is toast.message (info), but on failure toast.error also fires — meanwhile the info toast may still be visible. Consider dismissing the info toast on success/error to avoid stacked/duplicate messages during a 1-2 min manufacture.
MetricCard 'Formats' (line 77) has no accent; the two audio/video cards have gold/royal accents. Minor visual inconsistency — a subtle 'navy' accent would match the sidebar palette and Panel headers.

BACKEND = process.env.REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is read at module scope (line 11) with no fallback. If the env var is missing at build time, <audio>/<video> src becomes 'undefined/api/…' silently. Non-blocking today but a runtime guard/warning would be cleaner (same pattern flagged in iteration_72 review).

The truthful technique line for audio ('OpenAI narration (TTS)', 'Narrated host episode (TTS)') is good, but the audio panel does NOT include the same 'not frame-by-frame animation' truthfulness banner that the video panel implies through PageHeader. Consider surfacing a per-panel one-liner like 'Real OpenAI TTS · no synthetic voice cloning' on cs-audio for symmetric governance messaging.

cs-productions-list renders newest-first from the backend (Podcast Episode appeared at top after manufacture), but there is no visual 'NEW' badge, animation, or auto-scroll to the new row. On a long list, the Founder may not notice the new production without scrolling. A short-lived 'just made' badge or scroll-into-view would improve feedback.
